target_audience_note: The document names no customer segment. It describes cover for the insured person's private sphere: internet protection is granted "against computer risks or risks related to the use of the Internet in the context of their private life", home assistance applies "To the address of the risk indicated in the special conditions of the contract, located in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg" with extensions "in the event of relocation, temporary moving of furniture, student accommodation or holiday residence", and travel cancellation cover names "the insured person, their his spouse, the person with whom the insured person lives in a legal partnership or a member of their family who usually lives in their home".
summary: Insurance Product Information Document (IPID) for the "Personal Services" component of the easyPROTECT contract of LALUX Assurances. The document states that "The subscription of an easyPROTECT contract entitles you to certain exclusive services, in particular the possibility of benefiting, against payment of the corresponding premiums, from the guarantees described below." Four guarantee blocks are described: annual travel insurance (cancellation and interruption costs), annual assistance (medical care abroad, repatriation, early return, search and rescue), home assistance (24/7 emergency trades) and internet protection (loss of computer data and online purchases). The contract is annual with tacit renewal.

gaps: BRANCH DIVERGENCE — the task metadata gives `branch: multirisque-professionnelle` and the published filename reads `ipid_services-a-la-personne_lalux_easyprotect_en.pdf`, but the document itself describes private-lines cover only: internet protection is granted against risks "in the context of their private life", home assistance applies to "the address of the risk indicated in the special conditions of the contract, located in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg" with extensions for "relocation, temporary moving of furniture, student accommodation or holiday residence", and travel cancellation covers the insured person, spouse, legal partner and family members living in their home. Nothing in the document mentions a professional activity, business premises or a trade sector. The French phrase "services à la personne" in the filename can also denote a professional sector, which is the likely origin of the metadata. `branch` has therefore been set to `autres`, the document being a bundle of four heterogeneous guarantees (annual travel insurance, annual assistance, home assistance, internet protection) that fits no single branch slug; a reviewer preferring the dominant guarantee would set `voyage`. The document itself never names a branch.
`target_audience` is null: the document names no customer segment. Its own wording about the private sphere is kept verbatim in `target_audience_note` rather than converted into a category.

Carrier: the document prints the brand "LALUX Assurances" in the title banner ("LALUX Assurances - Product : easyPROTECT - Personal Services") and refers throughout to "the Company" / "the company" without ever naming a legal entity. No legal form, no RCS number, no address and no authorisation appear on the document, so it is not possible to tell from this document alone which of the group's authorised entities carries the risk. `insurer_name` reproduces the brand as printed.

No edition date is printed anywhere on the document: `edition_date` is null. The PDF metadata carries a creation date of 2018-10-08 and the InDesign file name "IPID_Services à la personne_LALUX_easyPROTECT_EN.indd"; these are metadata, not printed statements, and were not used.

Insurer's own wording kept verbatim, not corrected: "Sickness, bodily injury or death of the insured person, their his spouse" ("their his"), and "the company can suspend the warranties" ("warranties" for guarantees). Both were checked on a render of the page and are genuinely printed that way.

Product name: the document prints two forms — the title banner reads "Personal Services" and the blue product line reads "LALUX Assurances - Product : easyPROTECT - Personal Services". The fuller printed form was taken as `product_name`, with `product_family` = easyPROTECT and `variant` = Personal Services. "easyPROTECT" is a commercial range, not a branch, and was not used to classify the document.

The four guarantee blocks are printed as headings without ticks ("Annual travel insurance", "Annual assistance", "Insured event", "Guaranteed services", "Home assistance", "Internet protection"); only the individual items below them carry a green tick. `coverages` follows the ticked items, each description carrying its block heading so the structure is not lost.

The three items in the "Are there any restrictions on cover?" box that carry figures (maximum three interventions per year, guarding for a maximum of 72 hours, goods worth between EUR 150 and EUR 5,000) are restrictions rather than exclusions in the strict sense. They are kept in `exclusions` where the document prints them, and the same figures are additionally reflected in the `limits` / `sub_limits` / `conditions` of the guarantees they restrict; these are not additional distinct items.
Both the "What is not insured ?" and the "Are there any restrictions on cover?" boxes carry the printed statement "Non-exhaustive list".

No deductible/franchise, no waiting period and no prescription period appear anywhere in the document: `deductibles`, `waiting_periods` and `prescription_period` are null/empty because the document is silent, not because they were not extracted. All amounts are printed as "EUR 50,000", "EUR 5,000", "EUR 150" — the € glyph does not occur in the document, so no currency symbol was lost.

Geometric check performed: the flat text emits the two boxes (y ≥ 251) before the top-of-page blocks (disclaimer at y 130, "What type of insurance is it ?" at y 208), so the flat reading order does not follow the printed vertical order. Attachment was rebuilt by column: x0 ≈ 31–45 (x1 ≤ 285) for the "What is insured ?" box, x0 ≈ 314–328 for "What is not insured ?" (y 251–526) then "Are there any restrictions on cover?" (y ≥ 543). No column reversal, no exclusion landing among the guarantees or the reverse; confirmed on a render.

The bullet marks (green ticks, red crosses, orange exclamation marks) are placed images (18 image blocks on page 1) and produce no text; their polarity was read from the render and matches the heading of the box that carries them. These findings are not in `key_quotes` because they are not text.

The prompt text was verified against the local PDF: both pages come out character-for-character identical from `page.get_text("text")`. No truncation, no private-use-area glyphs, no U+0007, no zero-width spaces, no soft hyphens, no lost ligatures.

This document is one of several language versions of the same product published by lalux. It was extracted from its own English text only; no wording, amount or missing field was completed from a French or German sibling.
